teaching.hint: Can two arrivals at the same point but in different lanes be treated as equivalent?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The future depends on both position and lane; retaining a best cost for each of only three lanes avoids path enumeration.
solution_outline.approach: Process points in order. Carry valid straight movements forward, then account for legal same-point side jumps among open lanes, retaining the cheapest cost per lane.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: For each point and lane, the state is the least side jumps needed to stand there after any permitted jumps at that point.
solution_outline.correctness: Every path reaches a point by a straight move from the previous point, possibly followed by a side jump; the transitions cover these choices. Repeated same-point jumps cannot improve on one direct jump.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space because there are only three lanes.
solution_outline.pitfall: A side jump cannot land on the lane blocked at the point where it occurs.

common_wrong_turns: Choose one lane greedily for the whole trip
Ignore which point a lateral jump occurs at
source_fidelity_notes: The single-obstacle rule, any-lane finish, nonadjacent side jump, and open endpoints are explicit.
